Anderson: Clinton is the county seat of Anderson County, Tennessee. Oak Ridge — the Manhattan Project's Atomic City — and TVA's Norris Dam still define the county west of Knoxville.
Bedford: Shelbyville is the county seat of Bedford County, Tennessee. Shelbyville bills itself as the Walking Horse Capital of the World; the Tennessee Walking Horse National Celebration is the local institution.
Benton: Camden is the county seat of Benton County, Tennessee. Camden sits on Kentucky Lake, one of the largest man-made lakes in the United States, on the Tennessee River.
Bledsoe: Pikeville is the county seat of Bledsoe County, Tennessee. Pikeville is the only incorporated town; the rest is Cumberland Plateau farmland, timber, and Fall Creek Falls country.
Blount: Maryville is the county seat of Blount County, Tennessee. Maryville and Alcoa sit at the western door of Great Smoky Mountains National Park; Alcoa was built as a company aluminum town.
Bradley: Cleveland is the county seat of Bradley County, Tennessee. Cleveland is a manufacturing town on the Ocoee corridor and home to Lee University.
Campbell: Jacksboro is the county seat of Campbell County, Tennessee. Jellico and LaFollette grew as coal and railroad towns on the Kentucky line; I-75 climbs the plateau here.
Cannon: Woodbury is the county seat of Cannon County, Tennessee. Woodbury sits under Short Mountain and is long known for country music, crafts, and the short-lived but famous Cannon County music scene.
Carroll: Huntingdon is the county seat of Carroll County, Tennessee. Huntingdon is the seat of this West Tennessee farm county between Jackson and Paris.
Carter: Elizabethton is the county seat of Carter County, Tennessee. Elizabethton's Sycamore Shoals is where the Watauga Association and the Overmountain Men organized before Kings Mountain.
Cheatham: Ashland City is the county seat of Cheatham County, Tennessee. Ashland City sits on the Cumberland River just northwest of Nashville, with Cheatham Lake and fast-growing subdivisions.
Chester: Henderson is the county seat of Chester County, Tennessee. Henderson is home to Freed-Hardeman University, a Churches of Christ campus in rural West Tennessee.
Claiborne: Tazewell is the county seat of Claiborne County, Tennessee. Tazewell and Harrogate sit under Cumberland Gap, the historic pass into Kentucky and Virginia; Lincoln Memorial University is in Harrogate.
Clay: Celina is the county seat of Clay County, Tennessee. Celina sits at the head of Dale Hollow Lake, famous for record smallmouth bass.
Cocke: Newport is the county seat of Cocke County, Tennessee. Newport on the French Broad is a gateway to Cosby and the eastern Smokies, with a long moonshine-and-tourism reputation.
Coffee: Manchester is the county seat of Coffee County, Tennessee. Manchester and Tullahoma share Arnold Air Force Base; Bonnaroo is held on a farm outside Manchester.
Crockett: Alamo is the county seat of Crockett County, Tennessee. Alamo is a cotton-and-soybean county seat in the West Tennessee bottomlands, named for Davy Crockett.
Cumberland: Crossville is the county seat of Cumberland County, Tennessee. Crossville sits high on the Cumberland Plateau and has become one of Tennessee's largest retirement and golf communities — this is not Cumberland County, North Carolina.
Davidson: Nashville is the county seat of Davidson County, Tennessee. Nashville is the county: state capital, country music, health care, and tourism stacked on the Cumberland River.
DeKalb: Smithville is the county seat of DeKalb County, Tennessee. Smithville hosts the Smithsonian-recognized Fiddlers' Jamboree and sits on Center Hill Lake.
Decatur: Decaturville is the county seat of Decatur County, Tennessee. Decaturville and Parsons sit on the west bank of Kentucky Lake / the Tennessee River in rural West Tennessee.
Dickson: Charlotte is the county seat of Dickson County, Tennessee. Dickson and Charlotte sit on the western approach to Nashville along I-40; the county is a classic Middle Tennessee exurb.
Dyer: Dyersburg is the county seat of Dyer County, Tennessee. Dyersburg is a Mississippi River-bottom manufacturing town in Tennessee's northwest corner.
Fayette: Somerville is the county seat of Fayette County, Tennessee. Somerville is the seat of a fast-growing Memphis exurb of horse farms and new subdivisions.
Fentress: Jamestown is the county seat of Fentress County, Tennessee. Jamestown is Sgt. Alvin C. York country, with Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area to the north.
Franklin: Winchester is the county seat of Franklin County, Tennessee. Winchester and Sewanee — the University of the South — sit under the Cumberland Plateau escarpment near the Alabama line.
Gibson: Trenton is the county seat of Gibson County, Tennessee. Trenton, Humboldt, and Milan make up a cluster of West Tennessee railroad and manufacturing towns; Trenton is known for its teapots.
Giles: Pulaski is the county seat of Giles County, Tennessee. Pulaski, on the Elk River just north of the Alabama line, is unfortunately also known as the birthplace of the Ku Klux Klan in 1865.
Grainger: Rutledge is the county seat of Grainger County, Tennessee. Rutledge is known statewide for tomatoes and beans; Cherokee Lake forms the southern edge of the county.
Greene: Greeneville is the county seat of Greene County, Tennessee. Greeneville was home to President Andrew Johnson and is one of the state's oldest towns; Tusculum University is nearby.
Grundy: Altamont is the county seat of Grundy County, Tennessee. Altamont sits on the plateau; the county is known for South Cumberland parks and a 19th-century Swiss colony at Gruetli-Laager.
Hamblen: Morristown is the county seat of Hamblen County, Tennessee. Morristown is an industrial and rail town in the Holston Valley and a long-time manufacturing hub of East Tennessee.
Hamilton: Chattanooga is the county seat of Hamilton County, Tennessee. Chattanooga, between Lookout Mountain and the Tennessee River, is the county — freight, tourism, and a rebuilt downtown.
Hancock: Sneedville is the county seat of Hancock County, Tennessee. Sneedville is one of Tennessee's most isolated seats, in the Clinch Mountains, with a well-known Melungeon heritage.
Hardeman: Bolivar is the county seat of Hardeman County, Tennessee. Bolivar sits on the Hatchie River in rural Southwest Tennessee, a cotton-and-timber county east of Memphis.
Hardin: Savannah is the county seat of Hardin County, Tennessee. Savannah is the gateway to Shiloh National Military Park on the Tennessee River, site of the 1862 battle.
Hawkins: Rogersville is the county seat of Hawkins County, Tennessee. Rogersville claims Tennessee's oldest courthouse and newspaper, on the Holston River in the Tri-Cities region.
Haywood: Brownsville is the county seat of Haywood County, Tennessee. Brownsville is a cotton-belt seat west of Jackson, with a historic Black music and civil-rights story — Sleepy John Estes country.
Henderson: Lexington is the county seat of Henderson County, Tennessee. Lexington sits between Jackson and Natchez Trace country; Natchez Trace State Park is the local landmark.
Henry: Paris is the county seat of Henry County, Tennessee. Paris, home of the World's Biggest Fish Fry, sits near Paris Landing State Park on Kentucky Lake.
Hickman: Centerville is the county seat of Hickman County, Tennessee. Centerville on the Duck River is a timber and rural Middle Tennessee seat on the western Highland Rim.
Houston: Erin is the county seat of Houston County, Tennessee. Erin is one of the state's smallest county seats, in the hills between the Tennessee and Cumberland rivers.
Humphreys: Waverly is the county seat of Humphreys County, Tennessee. Waverly, on the Duck River, was the site of the catastrophic August 2021 flood that destroyed much of downtown.
Jackson: Gainesboro is the county seat of Jackson County, Tennessee. Gainesboro sits on Cordell Hull Lake where the Roaring River meets the Cumberland — this is Jackson County, Tennessee, not Mississippi.
Jefferson: Dandridge is the county seat of Jefferson County, Tennessee. Dandridge, one of the state's oldest towns, sits on Douglas Lake along I-40 between Knoxville and Morristown.
Johnson: Mountain City is the county seat of Johnson County, Tennessee. Mountain City is Tennessee's northeasternmost seat, high in the Unaka Mountains on the North Carolina and Virginia lines.
Knox: Knoxville is the county seat of Knox County, Tennessee. Knoxville — the University of Tennessee, the 1982 World's Fair, and TVA's historic headquarters — sits in the Great Valley.
Lake: Tiptonville is the county seat of Lake County, Tennessee. Tiptonville sits on Reelfoot Lake, formed by the 1811–12 New Madrid earthquakes, in the state's northwest corner on the Mississippi.
Lauderdale: Ripley is the county seat of Lauderdale County, Tennessee. Ripley is the seat; Fort Pillow State Historic Park stands on the Mississippi River bluffs north of Memphis.
Lawrence: Lawrenceburg is the county seat of Lawrence County, Tennessee. Lawrenceburg, on Shoal Creek, is David Crockett country and a manufacturing town near the Alabama line — not Lawrence County, Kentucky.
Lewis: Hohenwald is the county seat of Lewis County, Tennessee. Hohenwald is near the Natchez Trace and the grave of Meriwether Lewis, who died at Grinder's Stand in 1809.
Lincoln: Fayetteville is the county seat of Lincoln County, Tennessee. Fayetteville sits on the Elk River just above the Alabama line; the county is rural Middle Tennessee farm country.
Loudon: Loudon is the county seat of Loudon County, Tennessee. Loudon and Lenoir City sit on Fort Loudoun and Tellico lakes, TVA impoundments of the Tennessee River southwest of Knoxville.
Macon: Lafayette is the county seat of Macon County, Tennessee. Lafayette is a rural Upper Cumberland seat north of Gallatin, on the Kentucky line.
Madison: Jackson is the county seat of Madison County, Tennessee. Jackson is West Tennessee's mid-size hub — rail, hospitals, Casey Jones, and Union University.
Marion: Jasper is the county seat of Marion County, Tennessee. Jasper sits where the Cumberland Plateau meets the Tennessee River near Nickajack Lake and the Sequatchie Valley mouth.
Marshall: Lewisburg is the county seat of Marshall County, Tennessee. Lewisburg is a manufacturing seat south of Nashville, long tied to the auto-parts belt and the Tennessee Walking Horse.
Maury: Columbia is the county seat of Maury County, Tennessee. Columbia and Spring Hill sit on the I-65 growth corridor; the GM Spring Hill plant (formerly Saturn) is the industrial anchor.
McMinn: Athens is the county seat of McMinn County, Tennessee. Athens is remembered for the 1946 Battle of Athens, when returning veterans overthrew a corrupt county political machine.
McNairy: Selmer is the county seat of McNairy County, Tennessee. Selmer is Buford Pusser country — the Walking Tall sheriff — on the Mississippi line in Southwest Tennessee.
Meigs: Decatur is the county seat of Meigs County, Tennessee. Decatur is a small seat on Watts Bar Lake, between Cleveland and Kingston, one of Tennessee's smallest counties.
Monroe: Madisonville is the county seat of Monroe County, Tennessee. Madisonville and Tellico Plains sit under the Unicoi Mountains; the Cherohala Skyway starts here.
Montgomery: Clarksville is the county seat of Montgomery County, Tennessee. Clarksville, on the Cumberland, is Tennessee's fifth-largest city and the civilian neighbor of Fort Campbell — not Montgomery, Alabama.
Moore: Lynchburg is the county seat of Moore County, Tennessee. Lynchburg is home to the Jack Daniel Distillery; Moore is one of Tennessee's smallest counties and a consolidated city-county.
Morgan: Wartburg is the county seat of Morgan County, Tennessee. Wartburg sits by Frozen Head State Park; the old Brushy Mountain State Penitentiary is at Petros.
Obion: Union City is the county seat of Obion County, Tennessee. Union City is the seat of this northwest farm and manufacturing county near Reelfoot Lake, on the Kentucky line.
Overton: Livingston is the county seat of Overton County, Tennessee. Livingston is the Upper Cumberland seat by Standing Stone State Park, north of Cookeville.
Perry: Linden is the county seat of Perry County, Tennessee. Linden is one of the least-populated seats, on the Buffalo River in the Western Highland Rim.
Pickett: Byrdstown is the county seat of Pickett County, Tennessee. Byrdstown sits on Dale Hollow Lake in Tennessee's Upper Cumberland, the state's least-populous county.
Polk: Benton is the county seat of Polk County, Tennessee. Benton sits on the Ocoee River — site of Olympic whitewater — and the old Copper Basin mining district.
Putnam: Cookeville is the county seat of Putnam County, Tennessee. Cookeville, home of Tennessee Tech, is the Upper Cumberland's main town on I-40 between Nashville and Knoxville.
Rhea: Dayton is the county seat of Rhea County, Tennessee. Dayton hosted the 1925 Scopes 'Monkey' Trial; Watts Bar Lake forms the eastern edge of the county.
Roane: Kingston is the county seat of Roane County, Tennessee. Kingston, at the Clinch and Tennessee confluence, sits next to Oak Ridge and Watts Bar; Harriman and Kingston are the river towns.
Robertson: Springfield is the county seat of Robertson County, Tennessee. Springfield is a tobacco and manufacturing seat on I-24 / I-65 north of Nashville, historically one of the dark-fired tobacco capitals.
Rutherford: Murfreesboro is the county seat of Rutherford County, Tennessee. Murfreesboro — MTSU and the geographic center of the state — and Smyrna's Nissan plant make this one of Tennessee's fastest-growing counties.
Scott: Huntsville is the county seat of Scott County, Tennessee. Huntsville is the seat of Big South Fork country on the Kentucky line; the county once briefly seceded as the 'Free and Independent State of Scott.'
Sequatchie: Dunlap is the county seat of Sequatchie County, Tennessee. Dunlap sits in the narrow Sequatchie Valley between plateau walls, a coal-and-farm county northwest of Chattanooga.
Sevier: Sevierville is the county seat of Sevier County, Tennessee. Sevierville, Pigeon Forge, and Gatlinburg are the tourist strip into Great Smoky Mountains National Park, Tennessee's most-visited destination.
Shelby: Memphis is the county seat of Shelby County, Tennessee. Memphis, on the Mississippi, is the county — river freight, St. Jude, Beale Street, and the state's largest city.
Smith: Carthage is the county seat of Smith County, Tennessee. Carthage, on the Cumberland, was the longtime home of the Gore family and a classic Middle Tennessee river town.
Stewart: Dover is the county seat of Stewart County, Tennessee. Dover is the seat of Fort Donelson National Battlefield and the Tennessee side of Land Between the Lakes.
Sullivan: Blountville is the county seat of Sullivan County, Tennessee. Blountville is the seat; Kingsport, Bristol, and the Tri-Cities industrial belt are the population — Eastman and the Birthplace of Country Music.
Sumner: Gallatin is the county seat of Sumner County, Tennessee. Gallatin is the seat; Hendersonville and the Old Hickory Lake towns are Nashville's northern suburbs.
Tipton: Covington is the county seat of Tipton County, Tennessee. Covington is a Mississippi-bottom seat just north of Memphis, part of the Memphis metro farm-and-exurb belt.
Trousdale: Hartsville is the county seat of Trousdale County, Tennessee. Hartsville is Tennessee's smallest county by land area — a single-city county on the Cumberland, often called Hartsville/Trousdale County.
Unicoi: Erwin is the county seat of Unicoi County, Tennessee. Erwin sits on the Nolichucky in a narrow Appalachian valley on the North Carolina line, long a railroad and CSX shop town.
Union: Maynardville is the county seat of Union County, Tennessee. Maynardville is the seat of a Norris Lake county carved from five neighbors in 1850, now a Knoxville-exurb and lake county.
Van Buren: Spencer is the county seat of Van Buren County, Tennessee. Spencer sits above Fall Creek Falls, one of the highest waterfalls in the eastern United States.
Warren: McMinnville is the county seat of Warren County, Tennessee. McMinnville calls itself the Nursery Capital of the World; the county is the center of the Southern ornamental-nursery trade.
Washington: Jonesborough is the county seat of Washington County, Tennessee. Jonesborough is Tennessee's oldest town; Johnson City is the population and medical center of the Tri-Cities — not Washington state or D.C.
Wayne: Waynesboro is the county seat of Wayne County, Tennessee. Waynesboro is a sparsely settled Highland Rim seat on the Alabama line along the Natchez Trace.
Weakley: Dresden is the county seat of Weakley County, Tennessee. Dresden is the seat; Martin is home to the University of Tennessee at Martin in the state's northwest farm belt.
White: Sparta is the county seat of White County, Tennessee. Sparta sits under the Cumberland Plateau near Rock Island State Park and the Caney Fork.
Williamson: Franklin is the county seat of Williamson County, Tennessee. Franklin and Brentwood are among the wealthiest suburbs in the South, south of Nashville on I-65, with a major Civil War battlefield in Franklin.
Wilson: Lebanon is the county seat of Wilson County, Tennessee. Lebanon is the seat; Mount Juliet is the fast-growing Nashville-edge city along I-40 east, home to a big Amazon air hub.
